original_request: Propose a sequencing assay that jointly measures newly synthesized RNA and cell-surface protein identity in individual cells, with existing sequencing equipment. Investigate whether this capability is already demonstrated. If it is, identify a specific useful improvement over the closest implementation rather than presenting the combination itself as new. Return a proposed assay architecture as a State–Operation–Flow graph, the proposed change, its experimental precedents, unresolved interfaces and a discriminating experiment.
interpreted_goal:
Develop two independent, mechanistically distinct proposals for a sequencing assay that attributes newly synthesized RNA and cell-surface protein identity to the same individual cell using existing sequencing equipment. A useful biological measurement would relate a cell's recent gene-specific RNA production over a stated labeling window to its measured surface phenotype. Each expert must explain the biological quantity, molecule acted on, physical carrier of each association, direct instrument observations, and subsequent inference. New-RNA counts or fractions are useful endpoints; synthesis/degradation rates need additional sampling and model assumptions. Identify a useful physical design improvement, rather than treating an application, computational inference, or juxtaposition of existing assays as a new architecture.

First establish the closest implementation from primary evidence. The coordinator's bounded atlas and literature inspection verified component precedents but did not verify a same-cell newly-synthesized-RNA/surface-protein implementation. This is an unresolved search question, not evidence that the capability is absent. CITE-seq demonstrates co-capture and cell attribution of mRNA and antibody DNA reporters: atlas record_id=cite_seq, extraction_sha256=3316ec994882191444a4d6ab13edaf3f97562e4d9ca00642b6f061000a34b824, node_id=illumina:cite_seq:operation:lyse_capture. Its pinned primary source, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5669064/, source_id=primary:paper:28759029, text sha256=17170e847748ca17612bb02ef9d5677c8e4ddb9c50a1bd711d419713a97c0718, locator=[b00014]-[b00015] (inspected character window 2810-7810), reports shared cell indexing and species-mixing validation; short literal quote: 'both cellular mRNAs and antibody-derived oligos anneal to polyT-containing Drop-seq microparticles'. This supports the reported reporter/RNA association, not compatibility with a new RNA-labeling or processing interface.

Two literature starting points support distinct research directions. The registered scNT-seq2 report, https://www.ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC12157559/fullTextXML, source_id=literature:aa87bea57dc1d035cf42274b9893c67d950b077aa11c1644190d9f35d0a71f94, content_sha256=da11c22dfc2ccefe3276c7ef1642717a1b3360e8c1f15373e915bcae11d1ceba, locator=[b00007]-[b00015], describes second-strand primer/polymerase changes and comparative K562 results; short literal quote: 'increased library complexity (Fig. 1e), and reduced background mutation rates (Fig. 1f)'. These improvements are already reported and cannot themselves be presented as newly invented; their transfer to a joint assay would need evidence. The scEU-seq primary paper, https://www.hubrecht.eu/app/uploads/2017/11/VanOudenaarden_SCIENCE2020.pdf, source_id=literature:f26d37df98bc5db86c29dcfee4667e71b9fb43ff3f7373f37d739c9785858092, content_sha256=8fbae81d1fdb9a8fcdd733c05f29453799dac7b772a7740639ee5e6156546f56, locator=page 1, paragraph beginning 'To measure newly synthesized transcripts' and Fig. 1A (registered text window 4214-8714), reports in-situ EU biotinylation, cell-barcoded RNA/cDNA hybrids, pooling, and labeled/unlabeled separation; short literal quote: 'streptavidin magnetic beads'. This establishes a physical RNA-selection precedent, not surface-protein compatibility. The PDF text is registered as an excerpt; its column layout requires reading the indicated paragraph carefully, and uninspected supplementary details are unresolved.

Both experts must independently extend the prior-art search, including competing implementations and contrary interface evidence. If joint capability is demonstrated, use the closest implementation as the baseline and identify a specific useful before/after physical change. Otherwise distinguish a proposed integration from a novelty claim. Compare relevant outcomes such as correctly attributed new-RNA molecules per cell at matched sequencing effort, false new-RNA calls, protein-marker discrimination, cell recovery, cost, and throughput; state tradeoffs without inventing target performance. Each expert must deliver a complete starting-specimen-to-interpretable-readout State–Operation–Flow architecture, including an explicit sequencing operation and data state, a physical design change, scoped experimental precedents, unresolved interfaces, and a discriminating experiment. Track cell identity, RNA-label status, gene identity, protein-target identity, and molecular counting where claimed through every relevant separation, copying step, and pooling event. Use the runner's candidate schema and distinguish demonstrated behavior from transfers and unsupported hypotheses for each exact state, property, operation, and flow; evidence for separate components does not demonstrate their proposed interface. The runner will obtain the two initial proposals independently, review their graphs together, and permit one revision per expert. This plan assigns mandates only; it does not execute those stages, select a winner, or assert validation.
assumptions: Requester-supplied preferences, retained as soft preferences rather than hard constraints: 'Prefer accessible reagents and laboratory equipment'; 'Preserve multiple mechanistically distinct ideas if justified'. The two required expert mandates explore distinct approaches; later review may assess whether both remain justified.

Working interpretation: newly synthesized RNA means RNA made during a defined experimental window and recoverable at sampling. The specimen, labeling strategy, window length, RNA classes, and required temporal resolution are unspecified. A run-on measurement of engaged polymerases or unspliced-RNA inference is a different quantity and must not be substituted without explaining the distinction.

Working interpretation: cell-surface protein identity can be a known target identified through a validated binding reagent and associated reporter. The requester did not demand de novo protein amino-acid sequencing, absolute copy numbers, or newly synthesized protein measurement. Antibody-derived sequence counts require specificity and background controls before interpretation as target abundance.

The explicit readout constraint requires sequencing to be included; it does not explicitly require every modality to be sequenced. A protein reporter may be sequenced, or an orthogonal protein observation may be linked to the same cell if justified. Neither expert is required to combine particular named methods.

No organism, specimen, cell type, minimum cell count, marker-panel size, budget, sequencing depth, or capture platform is specified. A tractable cultured-cell or mixed-cell benchmark is a possible initial test, not a requester requirement or proof of transfer to primary specimens. Genome-wide coverage and total-RNA measurement are useful options, not additional hard constraints.

Use existing sequencing equipment is a hard constraint. Custom upstream reagents, capture supports, fluidics, or other laboratory equipment are allowed in principle; disclose their availability, accessibility, engineering requirements, and effect on feasibility. Do not turn the equipment preference into a prohibition on new sample-preparation hardware.

Feasibility of metabolic labeling in a chosen specimen, preservation of relevant epitopes, reporter specificity and retention, RNA recovery, barcode attachment before identity-destroying pooling, and compatibility of chemical and enzymatic steps are questions to test, not established assumptions of success.

Evidence limits: lexical atlas matches are starting points, and missing records or connections do not establish novelty or lack of historical precursors. No historical absence claim is made. The original scNT-seq publisher/PMC page acquisitions returned challenge pages, and its Europe PMC XML acquisition failed; these captures are retrieval limitations and provide no scientific support. The scNT-seq2 report and scEU-seq passage above were actually registered and read. The checked passages do not establish the proposed joint interfaces.

experts.expertise: RNA metabolic labeling, chemical encoding of RNA age, reverse transcription and library chemistry, and single-cell molecular attribution. This is a reasoning responsibility, not a claim of laboratory competence.
experts.question: Can an assay encode recent RNA synthesis in sequence while retaining reliable surface-protein-to-cell attribution, with a concrete gain in new-RNA detection or joint measurement fidelity over the closest demonstrated implementation?
experts.approach:
Explore RNA-age information encoded as a recoverable sequence feature, together with a surface-protein measurement assigned to the same cell. Choose the label, encoding reaction, processing order, capture system, and protein readout from evidence; named method combinations are not prescribed. Start by checking primary demonstrations of this joint capability, including variants and supplements. Use CITE-seq's shared indexing as a component precedent and the registered scNT-seq2 report as a competing RNA-library improvement, without assuming their interfaces are interchangeable. Identify the actual bottleneck in the closest implementation: possible research targets include loss or biased recovery of converted RNA, unreliable short-window new-RNA discrimination, or loss/misassignment of protein reporters. Choose and justify a specific physical change to an operation, substrate, reporter, or capture interface; specify before/after materials and the expected measurable benefit. A new inference algorithm alone is insufficient.

Propose the entire workflow from a stated cell specimen through labeling and surface measurement, isolation, chemical processing, cell indexing, RNA-derived and reporter-derived products, sequencing on existing equipment, and cell-resolved interpretation. Explain when RNA and protein signals acquire their cell association and what physically carries it before and after pooling. If sequencing antibody tags, distinguish target protein, binding reagent, reporter DNA, and copied sequencing library; protein identity comes from the reagent-to-target map, not a sequenced protein molecule. Determine exactly which substrates and end groups the proposed reactions require and whether the reported evidence tests them in the proposed context. In particular, resolve exposure of reporters, capture oligos and RNA to encoding chemistry, cleanup carryover, effects on reverse transcription, and encoding errors versus genuine label-derived signal. Assign transfer or hypothesis status where the exact joint interface has not been demonstrated.

Design a discriminating comparison with the closest implementation using matched specimen and sequencing effort. Include controls that distinguish labeling, chemical/enzymatic background, and cell-attribution failure, such as unlabeled and encoding-omission samples, labeled/unlabeled RNA standards, marker-positive/negative cells, and mixed-species or otherwise independently identifiable cells where appropriate. Measure joint retention of informative RNA and protein signals, false age calls, reporter misassignment and recovery, rather than only the success of each branch separately. State what observation would falsify the claimed physical improvement and what tradeoff would limit its value. Report equipment implications and untested interfaces explicitly; do not supply invented operating settings or claim readiness.
experts.why_distinct: This mandate treats RNA age primarily as information encoded in the sequenced molecule and focuses on conversion/copying fidelity and shared attribution. The other mandate explores physical selection or routing as the principal design axis, so the experts investigate different readout mechanisms and failure modes rather than variants of the same conversion workflow.

experts.expertise: Selective capture and molecular partitioning, single-cell compartment and barcode design, surface-binding reporters, and quantitative recovery through multi-branch workflows. This is a reasoning responsibility, not a claim of laboratory competence.
experts.question: Can physical selection or routing of newly synthesized RNA improve the useful joint RNA/protein measurement, for example by allocating sequencing effort to recent RNA or separating incompatible processing, while retaining correct same-cell associations?
experts.approach:
Explore an architecture in which a selective physical association, enrichment, compartment, or routed branch distinguishes recently synthesized RNA from pre-existing RNA. This is an exploratory design axis, not a requirement to use EU, biotin, a particular bead, or a particular named platform. First investigate existing same-cell new-RNA/surface-protein demonstrations and relevant competing selective-capture implementations. The registered scEU-seq page-1 passage establishes cell indexing before pooled separation of labeled and unlabeled RNA/cDNA hybrids; it does not establish that a protein-reporter branch survives that process. An additional atlas starting point is record_id=bru_seq, extraction_sha256=1c80854616e05c84c8a0935160cc992e94c3ede7ae3bd826ccf866a9ccf4a3f1, node_id=illumina:bru_seq:operation:capture_rna; pinned source_id=bru-seq::paper:23973811, https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4009065/, text sha256=f5d46c56b623c49ec48bdc89a752c4f8a319e5fc81f5559d3432bce73b813fb1, locator=[b00006]-[b00007] in inspected window 2645-6145, short literal quote: 'Bru-containing RNA is specifically captured using anti-BrdU antibodies conjugated to magnetic beads'. This demonstrates bulk labeled-RNA capture, not efficient single-cell recovery or joint protein compatibility. Treat alternative affinity mechanisms as distinct mechanisms requiring their own evidence.

Choose a useful limitation of the closest implementation and propose a specific before/after physical change to selective capture, processing order, compartment design, branch separation, or reporter/cell indexing. Complete the path from starting cells and surface-protein association through RNA labeling, isolation, selection or routing, library formation, existing-equipment sequencing, and joint interpretation. Identify which molecule is selected at each step: RNA, RNA/cDNA hybrid, cDNA, or a deliberately associated reporter. If RNA carries the label but cDNA is sequenced, show the actual linkage or data encoding that connects the label-selected fraction to the sequenced molecule. Identify when the cell association becomes recoverable, what happens to unselected material and protein reporters, how branches are reunited by cell identity, and whether selection changes the meaning or denominator of reported RNA counts. A split population does not establish a joint single-cell measurement; an early same-cell split needs an explicit physical mapping. The physical selection mechanism and branch architecture are the design focus; simply transplanting a known enrichment into an unchanged application is insufficient without a justified useful change.

Test selection specificity and recovery, stability of any RNA/cDNA association under actual purification conditions, cross-fraction carryover, nonspecific capture of protein reporters, cell barcode leakage/collisions, and effects of fixation or permeabilization on the surface readout. Establish required substrate or linkage properties from experiments; mark extrapolations to single-cell input or joint chemistry as transfers or hypotheses. Propose an end-to-end discriminating comparison with the closest implementation at matched read budget and stated input, using appropriate no-label/no-selection controls, distinguishable labeled and unlabeled standards, marker-positive/negative cells, and independently identifiable mixed cells. Quantify correctly paired informative new-RNA and protein observations, selection bias, contamination and cell/molecule recovery. Distinguish apparent enrichment from a net gain in useful measurement and state a result that would reject the proposed advantage. Disclose extra preparation hardware and engineering needs while retaining compatibility with existing sequencing equipment.
experts.why_distinct: This mandate makes physical selection and the material path of label-linked molecules central, with recovery, fraction purity and branch-to-cell mapping as primary bottlenecks. It allows different labels, carriers and compartment schemes from the sequence-encoding mandate and must justify its own complete architecture and tradeoffs.
